html:
Model decisions, capacity and cancellation

The native loop acquires one complete decision before it dispatches a tool. Model context preparation, a logical inference reservation, an actual model-capacity lease, provider transport and decision acceptance are separate boundaries. Keeping them separate explains why a task can be accepted yet waiting, why a stopped response cannot execute, and why a provider failure does not leave a capacity slot permanently occupied.

This guide describes the decision and lease owners. Model Configuration defines route/profile settings; scheduling covers task and Activity resource admission; inference management covers managed endpoint processes. None of those is a second Agent decision loop.

Owners and data flow

Owner Responsibility
AgentLoop Own run progression; prepare turns, acquire decisions, dispatch accepted calls and publish waits or outcomes.
model_decision.py Prepare bounded model input, reserve the logical call, apply recovery rules, validate the complete response and return ready, retry or stop.
agent_turns.py Identify endpoint capacity, register cancellable I/O ownership, arbitrate leases and bridge scheduled clients and Main fallback.
MemoryAgentTurns Publish live Controller lease, phase and metric records in RAM transactions. The base adapter supports standalone SQLite stores.
LLM adapters Build and send the configured provider request, assemble streaming responses and retain transport diagnostics.
turn_dispatch.py Accept the decision under its generation fence and enter the applicable Activity, capability or native-control path.
flowchart TD Saved[Accepted run state, instructions and current observations] --> Context[Bounded messages and selected tool schemas] Context --> Reserve[Logical decision reservation and checkpoint] Reserve --> Lease[Controller and endpoint capacity admission] Lease --> Recheck[Revalidate input and selected model] Recheck --> Transport[Owned provider request] Transport --> Complete[Complete response and usage] Complete --> Validate[Envelope, tool names and argument validation] Validate --> Fence[Pause, Stop, steering and Gateway evidence fences] Fence --> Ready[Ready decision returned to AgentLoop] Ready --> Dispatch[Activity or direct dispatch owner] Cache[Verified read-procedure proposal] --> Fence Transport -.-> Preview[Bounded progress and eligible answer preview] Preview -.-> UI[Presentation only]

A cached read-procedure proposal can bypass a provider request, but it still enters ordinary decision/dispatch checks. It is not a cached external success; the execution-cache guide explains fresh execution. Private stream fragments cannot enter the dispatch path. The request lifecycle explains progress events and guarded answer previews.

One reserved provider decision

sequenceDiagram participant L as Owned AgentLoop participant D as Decision acquisition participant S as Run state authority participant A as Model-capacity owner participant P as Provider adapter L->>D: Acquire next decision D->>D: Prepare bounded context and check Pause D->>S: Reserve logical call and save checkpoint D->>A: Request capacity for captured endpoint loop While capacity is unavailable A->>A: Check cancellation, deadline and shutdown A->>A: Wait for invalidation or 500 ms fallback end A-->>D: Lease acquired D->>D: Recheck observations, selections and model identity D->>P: Send owned request with messages and schemas P-->>D: Complete response or typed failure D->>A: Release capacity in context cleanup D->>D: Record usage and validate complete response alt Decision remains current and valid D-->>L: Ready decision with acceptance fence L->>L: Enter the normal dispatch boundary else Existing recovery policy admits another attempt D->>S: Save rejection and bounded recovery state D-->>L: Retry through ordinary loop else Pause, Stop or terminal recovery outcome D-->>L: Stop, or propagate the failure end Note over S: Runtime publication and disk checkpoint are distinct Note over P: Provider response is a proposal, not an execution receipt

The logical call reservation precedes transport, including a request interrupted before or during inference. Waiting for capacity does not create extra model requests. The leased block revalidates observations because independent Activities, selected saved messages or a managed model route may have changed while waiting. Changed context invalidates an incompatible retained generation continuation; the runtime cannot pretend the earlier prefill still describes the request.

Normal model usage is recorded even when the eventual response is discarded or rejected. The canonical assistant history keeps role, content and tool_calls; provider reasoning/extensions are not copied into that journal. Recorded usage and bounded model observations remain distinct from exact tool receipts.

Capacity, fairness and endpoint identity

The shared admission function examines queued and active leases in one state transaction. The effective Controller bound is the smallest applicable active lease limit and candidate limit. Native calls clamp the supplied limit to 1–8. The configured model-family policy can also limit simultaneous calls to one endpoint. An endpoint blocked by the RAM inference manager cannot be admitted.

Endpoint identity hashes normalized scheme, hostname, effective port, path and query. Credentials and model names do not create separate capacity pools for the same route. Clients without an HTTP base URL have no endpoint-specific identity; Controller admission still applies when they have a run store.

flowchart TD Queue[Waiters ordered by queued time and lease identity] --> Head[Consider oldest waiter for each endpoint] Head --> Endpoint{Endpoint available and within limit?} Endpoint -->|No| Wait[Retain waiter and report capacity reason] Endpoint -->|Yes| Controller{Controller capacity available?} Controller -->|No| Wait Controller -->|Yes| Admit[Atomically mark selected lease active] Wait --> Other[Consider an eligible different endpoint] Other --> Endpoint Admit --> Call[Caller executes within lease] Call --> Release[Remove lease, update metrics and notify waiters]

A later request cannot overtake an older waiter for the same endpoint merely by declaring a larger Controller limit. A different eligible endpoint can pass a blocked head. Admission does not first occupy a Controller slot while waiting for an endpoint slot. Wait callbacks and timeline reporting run outside the admission transaction; observer errors cannot decide who receives capacity.

Scheduled tracing clients normally acquire their own lease. Native decision preparation explicitly delegates one lease through those wrappers, so nested wrapping does not count the same physical call twice. Main-route fallback releases the old endpoint lease before preparing and admitting the replacement route. If inference management changes the resolved endpoint after admission, the wrapper releases that lease and acquires the correct endpoint before calling the provider.

The native_execution_phases records are small projections, not a second task state machine. Saving an ordinary running checkpoint does not overwrite a live model phase. Lease snapshots report aggregate active/waiting counts and metrics; their optional request filter narrows phase rows only. completed in these metrics counts acquired lease lifetimes, including failed calls, not successful task completions.

Cancellation, deletion and restart

sequenceDiagram participant C as Task or conversation deletion participant A as AgentTurns participant S as Native state authority participant O as Registered socket owner participant W as Waiting or active caller C->>A: Revoke selected request or run leases A->>S: Remove matching leases and phase projections A->>S: Retain tombstones against future claims S-->>A: Commit publication A->>O: Cancel matching in-process I/O owners A->>W: Notify capacity waiters W->>W: Check cancellation or missing reservation W->>A: Exit leased context and release local registration opt Later claim for a deleted identity W->>S: Check owner inside admission transaction S-->>W: IOCancelled end Note over A,W: Inference capacity is separate from external job ownership

lease() reuses an inherited socket owner or creates one for its caller. It checks cancellation around the caller's block, unregisters on every exit and closes only the owner it created. Revocation is scoped to the repository path and RAM generation when present. Deleting a model owner can release admission before a slow worker returns; the stopped worker still cannot acquire a fresh lease under a tombstoned identity.

Ordinary steering and Stop have their own generation/cancellation owners; they should not be inferred from this deletion sequence. A superseded decision is discarded or handed off through the existing steering protocol before dispatch. Releasing a model lease never proves that a Shell process, Gateway job or other external effect has ended. Those claims require their physical lifecycle evidence.

In standalone SQLite operation, recovery removes only mechanically dead process owners and changes their dispatch/model phase to ready_to_resume. A process that cannot be inspected is conservatively treated as alive. The active RAM adapter does not scan or reap on each call: exclusive Controller bootstrap invalidates old model leases once. See state recovery for saved-generation limits.

Response rejection and recovery

Acquisition returns a ModelDecision: ready carries a proposal for dispatch; retry and stop authorize no invocation. Tool names are checked against the advertised catalog before accepting business arguments. An excluded or undiscovered name does not become authorized because its malformed JSON was corrected. Pause, Stop, steering and changed Gateway evidence can still withhold an otherwise well-formed response.

Recovery is conditional on the accepted policy and failure category. Existing owners handle context overflow, generation quality, output-budget growth, constrained protocol recovery and eligible retained final prose. Their saved allowances and decision/input epochs prevent a stale continuation from silently replenishing its retry budget. A retained generation continuation is consumed once and must match its input scope, growth epoch and prompt layout.

An interrupted or incomplete native stream is not blindly rerun through generic protocol recovery. Eligible terminal prose may enter the existing completion normalization checks; it cannot fabricate an execution receipt. Failures outside the applicable recovery allowance propagate to the loop's normal failure/publication boundary. No rejected proposal is executed merely to see whether it would have worked.
